narrative.northStar: The Operations Console in Siigo Blue.
narrative.overview:
Toolbox's portal is a working console for the Siigo accounting team — a place to dispatch automations, audit their outcomes, and operate on tabular data without leaving the browser. The visual language borrows from engineering and accounting tooling (issue trackers, ERP tables, terminal UIs): typography carries weight, borders carry structure, and Siigo blue owns the chrome while a cool gray canvas plus white cards carry the work. Density still wins over breathing room; every pixel should help a counter answer "what is the status of this run?" or "where is this anticipo?" without scrolling for context.

The system is bilingual in form (light/dark themes over the same tokens via Tailwind v4's @custom-variant dark) but monolingual in voice (Spanish UI). It runs on Tailwind v4's CSS-first tokens and shadcn/ui's new-york primitives, with IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono as the only typefaces. Light and dark themes are not equals aesthetically — light is the working canvas for daytime data entry, dark is the after-hours and reduced-glare default — but neither is louder than the other.
keyCharacteristics: Sober, professional, dense; information density wins over whitespace
Three-zone contrast: Siigo blue sidebar chrome / cool gray canvas / white cards. The brand owns the rail; the work owns the well.
Siigo blue is the single brand accent; chart colors break out only inside data viz
Type pair is fixed: IBM Plex Sans for prose, IBM Plex Mono for numerics, codes, and the brand mark
Borders are the primary structural device; shadows appear only on lifted surfaces (cards, dialogs, sheets)
Operate mode: every screen ships explicit loading, empty, error, and success states

rules.name: The Three-Zone Contrast Rule
rules.body: Every screen is composed of three concentric layers — Siigo blue sidebar, gray canvas, white cards. Each layer earns its color from its job: brand voice, work surface, container. Don't collapse two layers into the same color.

rules.name: The One-Voice Rule
rules.body: Siigo blue appears in roughly ≤10% of any given viewport (plus the sidebar, which earns its color from being brand chrome). It speaks for primary actions, the Toolbox mark, and focus rings. It never co-occurs with another bright fill on the same screen — a Siigo blue button next to a coral destructive button on the same row breaks the rule.

rules.name: The Chart-Only Hue Rule
rules.body: Hues other than Siigo blue exist exclusively inside data viz (chart slots 2–5 and KPI tone chips). Emerald/amber/sky/rose tones are status colors, not decorative accents; do not promote them into brand surfaces.

rules.name: The Slate-Blue Family Rule
rules.body: Neutrals and the primary accent share the cool blue hue family (235°–256°). Coral is the only escape hatch from this family, used solely for destructive intent.

rules.name: The Mono-Number Rule
rules.body: Whenever a number is stacked, sorted, or compared in a list, render it in IBM Plex Mono with `tabular-nums`. This includes KPI values, dates in tables, counts in pagination (`Mostrando 1–5 de 23 registros`), and percent suffixes.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Label Rule
rules.body: Any text ≤ 12px that introduces a section, column, or group is uppercase + tracked + semibold. Mixed-case small text is reserved for prose.

rules.name: The Single-Canvas Rule
rules.body: Each page renders inside exactly one max-width container (`max-w-7xl`). Nested max-widths are only allowed inside dialog/sheet content; never stack two global containers.

rules.name: The 768px Surface Flip Rule
rules.body: Below 768px, any surface that opens centered (Dialog) flips to a bottom-anchored Drawer; the sidebar flips from persistent to a Sheet overlay. There is no third behavior for intermediate widths.

rules.name: The Quiet-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows appear only on lifted surfaces (cards at rest, popovers, dialogs, sheets). Never on rows, list items, badges, sidebar items, or inputs.

rules.name: The Border-First Rule
rules.body: When a surface needs to be visually separated, default to a 1px `--border` before reaching for a shadow. The topbar uses a border-bottom; table rows use a border-bottom; cards use both a border and a `shadow-sm`. Hover states on table rows use `bg-muted/40`, never a shadow.

rules.name: The Eight-Pixel-Family Rule
rules.body: All radii are derived from `--radius: 0.5rem` (8px): 4 / 6 / 8 / 12 px. Do not introduce new radii — if a new surface doesn't fit one of these four steps, change the surface, not the scale.

rules.name: The Square-Chrome Rule
rules.body: The persistent chrome (topbar, sidebar rail, page edges) is square. Corners only soften inside the content well.

dos: Do render every numeric column with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` and prefer IBM Plex Mono for values that get sorted or summed.
Do reserve primary buttons for the single most important action on a surface; use outline for the dismiss/secondary action.

Do pair the project motion tokens (`--duration-enter` 210ms with `--easing-enter` cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); `--duration-exit` 150ms with `--easing-exit` cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1); `--duration-move` 400ms) for every new entrance and exit. Never introduce new durations.
Do ship loading, empty, error, and success states on every view that fetches or mutates data.
Do use Spanish for every user-facing string. The product is monolingual in Spanish; English is only acceptable in code identifiers.
Do maintain WCAG AA contrast in both themes.
donts: Don't introduce display fonts, oversized headlines, or marketing-style typography. The portal is operate-mode internal tooling; the brand mark uses mono, not display serif.
Don't add new gradients, glassmorphism, blur effects, or decorative drop shadows. The system is intentionally flat; the topbar is solid white, not a backdrop-blurred overlay.
Don't invent new radii. Stick to the 4 / 6 / 8 / 12 px scale derived from the 8px base.
Don't promote status tones (emerald / amber / sky / rose) into brand surfaces, primary actions, or sidebar/navigation. They are functional, not decorative.
Don't stack two filled buttons of different intents on the same row (e.g., a coral destructive button next to a primary CTA). Confirm destructive intent with an AlertDialog instead.
Don't use shadow as decoration on rows, list items, badges, or sidebar items. Shadows appear only on lifted surfaces (cards at rest, popovers, dialogs, sheets).
Don't break the 768px Surface Flip Rule: any centered modal-style surface must become a bottom-anchored Drawer below 768px. There is no third responsive behavior.

Don't let the topbar drift back to a translucent overlay. The white-on-canvas split is what makes the Three-Zone Contrast Rule work; a backdrop-blurred topbar collapses the canvas and the content well into one surface.
